clue.text: Walk casually in street wind behind

indicators.note: behind says the word for wind is placed after the street abbreviation

parts.note: to roll is to wind, as a cable rolls onto a drum

explanation.surface: Someone ambles along a road with a breeze at their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely amble on foot is exactly what a casual walk is; the word is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Where a course at university may take one, in some measure

definitions.text: Where a course at university may take one
definitions.meaning: a university course leads to a qualification such as a BA, literally this phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Studying leads one to a qualification, and the idiom also means partly or to some extent.

clue.text: Plain the man fell, being past it?

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
he is the man
a fell is a hill, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: A man tumbled on flat ground; perhaps he is too old?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' and 'fell' look like flat land and a tumble but give OVERT and HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means too old to be effective, the same as being past one's prime.

clue.text: Crease? Any number in sheets, etc

parts.note: a line is a crease, as on a face or fabric
N is the algebraic symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A housekeeper asks about wrinkles in a number of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed sheets, pillowcases and tablecloths are collectively household textiles of this name.

clue.text: Drink — a suitable one agent knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back says the run of words before it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: fit means suitable, as in fit for purpose
I is the Roman numeral for one
a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: Someone describes a drink, a fitting one, that an agent downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like downing a drink, but here it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser drink taken before a meal, such as sherry or vermouth, is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Round fruit, soft

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A description of a ripe fruit: round and soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby or rounded in shape, said of a figure or a cushion.

clue.text: Looter overlooking a person on horseback

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the letter a is left out

parts.note: a raider is a looter

explanation.surface: A plunderer looks down on a mounted figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' suggests looking down from above, but means disregarding the A.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sits on and controls a horse is described directly by this word.

clue.text: Found in Croatia, rare crown

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: An unusual crown was discovered in Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled ornamental headband, or the papal triple crown, is a kind of crown.

clue.text: Incompetent fool, the old man, mostly supported by a daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the following letters sit below
mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the old man is slang for one's father

explanation.surface: Dad, a hopeless idiot, mostly leans on his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim-witted, stupid person is called this informally, a synonym of an inept fool.

clue.text: On the blink, TV near bar

indicators.note: a set that is on the blink is malfunctioning, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The television is broken, and it is standing near the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or inn where drinks are served is a bar, an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Fashion icon ringing a doctor, part of circle

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the designer's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Mary Quant, the British designer credited with popularising the miniskirt

explanation.surface: A famous designer telephones a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests a phone call but means encircling: QU(A DR)ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of a circle, the sector bounded by two perpendicular radii, is a part of a circle.

clue.text: Raised in W Somerset, near busy resort town

indicators.note: in says the word for raised goes inside the jumbled letters
busy suggests bustling activity, so these letters are stirred about

parts.note: something raised is up

explanation.surface: Someone was brought up in the west of Somerset, close to a bustling seaside place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' jumbles the next two words to ESTONSERMARE, and 'in' takes the word for raised. The town is a seaside resort on the Somerset coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a well-known English seaside holiday destination on the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Out of bed, drunk is nervy

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone up and already drunk is jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and anxious, unable to relax, which is what nervy means in British usage.

clue.text: Best stretch of thoroughfare, lit extensively

indicators.note: stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The finest part of a road, brightly illuminated.
explanation.definitionFit: The select top group, the cream of anything, is the best.

clue.text: After having blundered, Italian succeeded

indicators.note: after says the Italian abbreviation comes behind the phrase for blundered

parts.note: to goof is to blunder, so made a goof means blundered
IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it with Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian triumphed after a series of mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a success of something, so it fits having succeeded.

clue.text: Film based on fact — it follows King George

indicators.note: follows says the word it comes after the royal abbreviation

parts.note: a story based on fact is true
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A film based on a true story, made after a royal one about King George.
explanation.definitionFit: True Grit is a 1969 Western starring John Wayne, remade by the Coen brothers in 2010.

clue.text: River and wood crossing area in kingdom

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the wood word goes across the area letter

parts.note: elm is a wood

explanation.surface: A river and a forest cut through a region of a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain ruled by a monarch is a synonym of kingdom.

clue.text: Quite popular act

parts.note: something popular is in, or fashionable
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a turn was a crowd-pleaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an emphatic reply, quite and this word both express strong agreement.

clue.text: Regard first at the crease as a big surprise?

parts.note: to eye is to regard
in cricket, the opening batsman is first at the crease, where the batter stands

explanation.surface: A batter who is first in watches the pitch, surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line where a cricket batsman stands; the first pair in are the openers.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that astonishes and enlightens someone is a big surprise.

clue.text: Queen showing restraint entertaining head of government, American

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the restraint word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: a rein is a restraint, as on a horse

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A monarch shows restraint while hosting a US head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, used in royal signatures and legal case names.

clue.text: Communist measure demonstrates undue bureaucracy

parts.note: red is a colloquial word for a communist
a tape is a measure

explanation.surface: A communist policy shows excessive paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official rules and formalities are named from the ribbon once used to tie legal documents.

clue.text: Unclear situation in neutral region

parts.note: grey is a neutral colour
an area is a region

explanation.surface: Someone describes an ambiguous position in a no-man's-land.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a matter not clearly falling into any category, an ill-defined situation.

clue.text: CD in comic — pal drops it off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic book's character discards a compact disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CD in comic' reads like a disc, but CD is the definition: Corps Diplomatique, seen on embassy car plates.
explanation.definitionFit: CD abbreviates the French Corps Diplomatique, the body of diplomats posted to a country.

clue.text: Smooth tree

definitions.meaning: to smooth wood with a carpenter's tool
a tall broad-leaved tree, common in London streets

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a carpenter's levelling tool used as a verb and a broad-leaved shade tree.

clue.text: Bulb lit, current not off

parts.note: a lamp that is lit is on
I is the physics symbol for electric current
something not off is on

explanation.surface: A light bulb is lit, the current not switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' points to a light bulb, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable that grows as a layered bulb underground.

clue.text: Type of necktie produced by a Caledonian

parts.note: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A style of neckwear made by a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide cravat-style neck scarf named after the racecourse is a type of necktie.

clue.text: Chapter on old Irish group of singers

explanation.surface: A cathedral chapter rests on old Irish singers.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised body of singers, as in a church, is this group.

clue.text: Answer: draw off small measure, if necessary

parts.note: to tap a barrel is to draw off its liquid
an inch is a small measure of length

explanation.surface: Instructions: reply, then pour off a little, if you must.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an emergency or when needed, so it matches if need be.

clue.text: Away goal causes upset

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A goal scored by the visiting team causes a shock result.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to hurt their feelings or affront them, the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Aquatic bird — it nested within banks of estuary for donkey's years

indicators.note: nested within means placed inside, so the bird and it go between the outer letters
banks are the outer edges, so this picks the first and last letters of estuary

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A water bird has nested on the shores of an estuary for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks of' gives E and Y, the outside letters of estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey's years is British slang for a very long time, and this word means endless time.

clue.text: Sappers, weary, go to bed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: Military engineers, worn out, turn in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in for the night is a common sense of this verb, besides leaving work.
